properties.name: flo2 settled that the connector surface is its own product-shaped tools, so most of what a connector needs is not reflow2's work — and two named things must NOT be built here
properties.statement:
FLO2 F28 corrects its own F27 the same day, after Anthony settled the architecture in flo2's graph: reflow2 stays an ENGINE and grows no authentication; flo2 is the OAuth 2.1 resource server; the connector surface is flo2's own outcome-shaped tools implemented USING reflow2, not reflow2's tools and not reflow2's tools filtered.

🛑 TWO THINGS THEY EXPLICITLY ASK NOT TO BE BUILT, and the reasoning is theirs and is good.
① NO CONNECTOR MODE, TOOL SUBSET OR ALLOW-LIST. Filtering 181 tools down to twelve 'still puts detect_gaps, scan_nodes and gap_to_prompt in front of somebody who came to design a greenhouse. Fewer of the wrong shape is not the right shape.' They cite published MCP guidance against converting endpoints 1:1 into tools and for intention-level capabilities. Their verdict on this surface: 'Its 181-tool surface is correct for what it is — an engine driven by a developer with a coding agent on a trusted network. Do not degrade it to serve a connector it should not be serving.'
② NO OAUTH IN REFLOW2. 'It would be the wrong layer. Identity is per-product; reflow2 has several consumers and flo2 is one.' Adding it would bake one consumer's identity model into a component the others deploy differently.

⭐ WHAT REMAINS ON REFLOW2, their list: the result shape (recorded separately), the protocol question (answered), and F24 and F25 from the earlier addendum, of which F24 is now MORE load-bearing because a product surface must classify correctly on somebody else's model with no system prompt to lean on.

AND TWO THINGS THEY ASK NOT TO BREAK: `ingest_step` being stateless with explicit handles, which matches the spec's stateful-tools guidance, and `isError: true` plus an explanatory sentence, which is what the spec wants so a model can self-correct.
